relationship.statement: A pendulum's period increases with the square root of its length and is unaffected by bob mass. At small angles the period stays nearly constant, while large swings add extra time.
assumptions: Gravity is fixed at Earth surface (9.81 m/s^2).
The rod is massless and rigid with no air drag or friction.
T_0 gives the small-angle period while exact motion is shown.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var g = 9.81; var refLen = 1.0; var refDeg = 20; var refMass = 1.0; var refPivotX = -1.55; var testPivotX = 0.55; var pivotY = 2.0; function solve(L, deg, time) { var rad0 = deg * Math.PI / 180; var omega0 = Math.sqrt(g / L); var k = Math.sin(rad0 * 0.5); var a = [1]; var b = [Math.cos(rad0 * 0.5)]; var c = [k]; var n = 0; while (n < 10 && Math.abs(c[n]) > 1e-13) { var an = 0.5 * (a[n] + b[n]); var bn = Math.sqrt(a[n] * b[n]); var cn = 0.5 * (a[n] - b[n]); n = n + 1; a.push(an); b.push(bn); c.push(cn); } var aN = a[n]; var K = Math.PI / (2 * aN); var period = (4 * K) / omega0; var u = omega0 * time; var v = K - u; var phi = Math.pow(2, n) * aN * v; for (var i = n; i >= 1; i--) { var ratio = (c[i] / a[i]) * Math.sin(phi); if (ratio > 1) ratio = 1; if (ratio < -1) ratio = -1; phi = 0.5 * (phi + Math.asin(ratio)); } var sinHalf = k * Math.sin(phi); if (sinHalf > 1) sinHalf = 1; if (sinHalf < -1) sinHalf = -1; var theta = 2 * Math.asin(sinHalf); var maxSpeed = 2 * Math.sqrt(g * L) * k; return { theta: theta, angleDeg: theta * 180 / Math.PI, period: period, maxSpeed: maxSpeed }; } var testRes = solve(inputs.length, inputs.startAngle, t); var refRes = solve(refLen, refDeg, t); var testX = testPivotX + inputs.length * Math.sin(testRes.theta); var testY = pivotY - inputs.length * Math.cos(testRes.theta); var refX = refPivotX + refLen * Math.sin(refRes.theta); var refY = pivotY - refLen * Math.cos(refRes.theta); var testSize = 0.22 + 0.68 * (inputs.mass - 0.5) / 2.5; var refSize = 0.22 + 0.68 * (refMass - 0.5) / 2.5; var weight = inputs.mass * g; var arrowLen = 0.16 * inputs.mass; var weightTipY = testY - arrowLen; var isLargeAngle = inputs.startAngle > 30; var isSamePeriod = Math.abs(testRes.period - refRes.period) / refRes.period < 0.015; var isShorter = inputs.length < refLen; return { testX: testX, testY: testY, testSize: testSize, testAngle: testRes.angleDeg, period: testRes.period, maxSpeed: testRes.maxSpeed, weight: weight, weightTipY: weightTipY, refX: refX, refY: refY, refSize: refSize, refAngle: refRes.angleDeg, refPeriod: refRes.period, isLargeAngle: isLargeAngle, isSamePeriod: isSamePeriod, isShorter: isShorter }; }

lesson.title: What Changes How a Pendulum Swings?
lesson.description: Compare a test pendulum beside a fixed 1 m reference as both swing over six seconds. Adjust rod length, bob mass, and release angle to see what changes the swing period.
lesson.instructions: Set Test rod length to 1.0 m and Release angle to 20 deg, then vary Test bob mass to verify the two waves stay in sync. Next change rod length and finally sweep Release angle up to 70 deg to spot when the small-angle approximation slows down.
lesson.goal: Pendulum period grows with the square root of rod length and stays unaffected by bob mass, while large release angles add extra time beyond the small-angle rule.
